title: Cornell sexual assault investigation: Here’s the latest as governor rebukes DA’s handling of the case | CNN
text:
Source: CNN

Outrage is building as the case involving a Cornell University student allegedly gang raped in a fraternity house in 2024 continues to garner national attention, with the state’s governor vowing she “will not allow anyone to sweep this case under the rug.”

Snapchatmessages, a Cornell disciplinary panel’s decision and a cache of documents from the university’s formal Title IX investigation obtained by The New York Times have shed new light on what may have happened in the fraternity house, Doe’s reported frame of mind at certain points throughout that night and how her understanding of the events changed as she processed her trauma in the weeks that followed.

Cornell is facing scrutiny because the university initially said campus police investigated the allegations in 2024 and “shared all investigatory information with the Tompkins County District Attorney’s Office.” But the school laterchanged its statement, now saying police investigated the allegations in 2024 and “shared the victim’s sworn statement and the Snapchat screenshot” with the DA’s office.

The DA previously said his office did not bring criminal charges because of Doe’s six-page statement. He later said his office had access to some Snapchat messages exchanged during the alleged assault in a group chat titled, “Chi Phi Actives.” Images of one Snapchat chain obtained by CNNincludea photo of Doe in a room at the fraternity house during the time she describes being assaulted.

Doe made an explicit allegation of rape in her interview that was not included in the six-page statement furnished to prosecutors, according to WCBS.

Although Doe did recount being hit and feeling emotionally coerced in the statement, it did not include some stronger language orallegationsshe used in her interview, according to The New York Times, citing documents it obtained.

Among the documents alsoobtained by the Times, were records showing the district attorney’s office declined to review any additional evidence gathered by the campus police department beyond the six-page statement signed by Doe.

A Cornell police investigator spoke to a member of the district attorney’s staff on November 25, 2024, about reviewing additional evidence, the Times said. By that time, university police had conducted more interviews and reviewed chat messages, the Times report said.

But prosecutors did not express interest in the additional evidence because they had decided that, based on Doe’s statement, “Criminal charges would not be pursued in this case,” a Cornell police investigator said in a note documenting the call.

When reached for comment, the district attorney staff member referred all questions to the district attorney, the Times reported.

Van Houten, the district attorney, told the Times by email that any additional records gathered by the Cornell police were “not pertinent to our analysis because we had Jane Doe’s comprehensive account of the events.”

CNN reached out to Van Houten’s office for comment Friday.

CNN obtained a copy of a heavily redacted, 99-page documentsummarizing key evidenceincluded in a Cornell disciplinary panel’s decision, which supports the Times’ findings about how Doe later came to understand the night’s events as assault. The panel’s decision details more than 50 interviews, including with six of the seven accused men.

The initial university investigation led to suspensions and expulsions for the accused students, according to Doe’s attorney, the barring of the fraternity chapter from campus and the launch of a sexual assault task force. Four of the Chi Phi fraternity members acknowledged having sexual contact with Doe but said their interactions had been consensual. The others denied participating in sexual encounters, the Times reported.

Amid the renewed investigation, court documents show a Chi Phi fraternity member named as a defendant in Doe’s civil suit has beenpetitioningNew York state courts to invalidate a university disciplinary decision that found him responsible for attempted sexual exploitation.

Cornell student groups are planninga protest on campus Mondayto “hold our university responsible,” according to anInstagram postfrom Students for a Democratic Cornell and several other campus organizations.

Help is available: For help in the US, call the National Sexual Assault Hotline at 1-800-656-4673 or chat 24/7 ononline.rainn.org.

CNN’s Holly Yan, Jessie Yeung, Gloria Pazmino, Jason Carroll, Alisha Ebrahimji and Jake Tapper contributed to this report.
